scope: Frontend session additions, generated contracts, regression-test boundaries, audit/design/repair records and evidence tooling

findings.title: Activity pagination failure hides Stop and an otherwise available report
findings.session_relation: New history pagination delays publishing the entire snapshot until every event page loads.
findings.trigger: Open/reopen a run with more than100 events. GET snapshot succeeds, but a subsequent events-page request fails.
findings.actual: setSnapshot is after the pagination loop. On first load currentRun remains null, so running is false and Stop is absent; a valid completed report likewise has no export controls. Every retry starts the same coupled read.
findings.impact: An activity-only outage can remove cancellation controls while authorized work continues, or prevent access to an already available result.
findings.proof: root/frontend-audit.test.tsx first two probes; root/frontend-probes-final.log (3 reproduced-behavior assertions passed). Independently source-reviewed by runtime reviewer.
findings.recommendation: Publish validated run/report state immediately. Load activity pages in a separate generation-fenced state with its own loading/error/retry controls; retain Stop and saved-result access independently of history completeness.
findings.caveat: The Stop endpoint remains available; a previously displayed snapshot is retained. This specifically affects first/reopen loading and the new pagination dependency, not every network outage.

findings.title: A transient assessment-read failure silently removes the attestation workflow
findings.session_relation: The new scoped-assessment effect swallows errors and has no dedicated retry state.
findings.trigger: A terminal live report loads successfully, but its one GET /assessments fails temporarily.
findings.actual: The catch does nothing; targets remain empty and the attestation section is not rendered. Switching Evidence/Overview does not retry because only runId/report.id drive the effect.
findings.impact: The advertised verification/readiness path disappears without telling the user why or offering recovery. Reload or a changed report identity is needed.
findings.proof: root/frontend-audit.test.tsx third probe: assessment request observed once, form/error absent, tab switches do not retry.
findings.recommendation: Represent loading/error/unsupported/success states for assessment targets and expose an explicit read retry without clearing typed input or resubmitting inference.
findings.caveat: No false attestation or extra paid request occurs; this is a recoverability/availability defect.

findings.title: Repair record generation can rebind old green logs to changed, invalid source
findings.session_relation: New finalize.py creates the completion claims and source/evidence manifests from independently read text logs.
findings.trigger: Keep previous successful logs, change source afterward, then run finalize.py again.
findings.actual: The generator parses successful-looking text, marks all17 rows verified and then hashes current source. It does not require matching test-start input hashes or check process exit receipts. In a temporary copy, invalid Python is rebound to2014 passing tests and all17 verified closures. The generated report also claims evaluation/scenario checks passed although their logs were absent from that temporary copy.
findings.impact: Future reports can certify code that the recorded commands never tested; a matching current source-manifest then appears to substantiate stale results.
findings.proof: root/probe_record_binding.py; root/record-binding-results.json. Actual existing logs and copied source were used; only the temporary copy was mutated.
findings.recommendation: Capture command, exit status, profile and immutable input manifest at execution start. Check the same inputs at completion and consume those bound receipts in finalization; reject missing/stale checks before writing closures. Keep source hashes separate from a claim that those sources were executed.
findings.caveat: The current2014/250 totals were independently rerun successfully in this audit. This demonstrates stale-log rebinding in the reporting tool, not that the original current totals were fabricated or that hashes can resist an operator rewriting every artifact.
